name: IL-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Foster holds a massive financial edge: $2.6M on hand versus about $14K for Walter
District leans Democratic by six points and Foster is an established incumbent
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public general-election polling, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Foster's incumbency, a six-point Democratic district lean, and a lopsided fundraising gap—$2.6 million on hand against under $14,000 for Walter, with no outside opposition—align with markets pricing his reelection near 96 percent, all supporting a Safe D outlook.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Foster or a sharply unfavorable national environment could narrow what is otherwise a comfortable margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Foster, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northern Illinois district that leans Democratic by six points. He enters the general election with an overwhelming financial advantage, having raised about $2.5 million and holding roughly $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Walter has raised about $420,000 with under $14,000 remaining. No outside groups are spending against Foster, and prediction markets price his reelection chances at about 96 percent.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the stark resource gap. Those factors all point the same direction, suggesting a comfortable Democratic margin in the high teens. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves some room for a shifting national environment to move the race more than current signals indicate.
